sentences.text: Prakash vs State Of Maharashtra on 10 September, 2015

Author: Chief Justice
Bench: Chief Justice, Arun Mishra
 1
 In The Supreme Court Of India
 Criminal Appellate Jurisdiction
 Criminal Appeal No.596 Of 2010
 Prakash ..Appellant(S)
 Versus
 State Of Maharashtra ..Respondent(S)
 O R D E R
1.

This appeal is directed against the judgment and order passed by the High Court of Judicature at Bombay, Bench at Aurangabad in Criminal Appeal No.388 of 1997, dated 17.04.2009.
2.

entities.text: High Court of Judicature at Bombay, Bench at Aurangabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
By the impugned judgment and order, the High Court has reversed the findings and conclusions rendered by the Trial Court and allowed the appeal filed by the State and held the appellant-herein guilty of the offence punishable under Section 2(ix)(d) read with Section 7(ii), punishable under Section 16(1)(a)(i), Rule 23 read with Section 7(ii), punishable under Section 16(1)(a)(ii) and Rule 50 read with Section 7(ii), punishable under Section 16(1)(a)
(ii) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (for short, the Act) and rules made thereunder and sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for six months and to pay fine of Rs.1,000/- and in default to suffer rigorous imprisonment for three months 3.
We have heard Shri Shivaji M. Jadhav, learned counsel for the appellant and Shri Nishant Katneshwarkar, learned counsel for the respondent-State.

4. Shri Shivaji M. Jadhav, learned counsel appearing for the appellant would submit that the appellant-accused was unrepresented before the High Court and in view of that, the High Court ought to have appointed an amicus curiae, if the accused was unable to engage a counsel for him.
5. We have gone through the judgment and order passed by the High Court.
In our view, when an accused was unrepresented before a Court, it was the duty of the Court to have appointed an amicus curiae to assist the accused.
Since that has not been done by the High Court in the instant case, we take exception to the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court.

sentences.text: Accordingly, we set aside the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court and remand the matter back to the High Court for fresh disposal in accordance with law.
7. If, for any reason, the accused is unable to have the assistance of a learned counsel, we request the High Court to appoint an amicus curiae to assist the appellant/ accused.
8. The Criminal Appeal is disposed of accordingly.
Ordered accordingly.
